public_rationale: The condition has not been established. Research measures substantial AI authorship and demonstrates that AI-written web text can enter training experiments. But AI-written material is not necessarily material written for robots; one relevant study explicitly concerns text written for human readers. Treating those categories as identical would change the claim. Under the conditional-forecast rule, an unknown antecedent prevents scoring the forecast. No deadline or decisive resolving event is present.
limitations: English-language webpage samples do not represent every kind of internet content.
AI detectors have classification errors and do not measure intended audience.
Experimental training inclusion does not establish prevalence across future commercial models.

statement.excerpt: I am not saying that user-generated content will disappear, but that human beings cannot create content at the scale that automation can, and when a large chunk of the internet is content for robots, that is the content that will inform tomorrow's models.
statement.document_title: Are We Watching The Internet Die?

our_interpretation: The forecast is conditional and has no deadline; tomorrow's models means subsequent model generations.
Content for robots means material primarily produced to satisfy automated ranking, crawling, or similar systems, consistent with the surrounding discussion.
AI authorship alone does not establish that content was written for robots rather than human readers.
Inform models means enter their training data and contribute to learned behavior, not merely be retrieved after training.
The scale comparison concerns production capacity, not a claim that automation had already produced more total content than all humans.
criteria.support_condition: After robot-targeted material demonstrably becomes a substantial share of web content, dated training records show that later models ingest and learn from that material. Production measurements also substantiate automation's greater scalable output capacity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Once the antecedent is established, representative subsequent training records show that the predicted material is effectively excluded and does not inform the relevant models. A temporary lack of examples would not disprove an undated forecast.

evidence.explanation: The sampled English-language web contains a measurable share of detector-identified AI writing. This does not measure whether those pages were primarily written for robots, so it does not establish the stated antecedent.

The study reports AI-labeled tokens surviving FineWeb filtering and experiments training models with that material. It expressly describes the web text studied as written for human readers, so it cannot substitute for evidence about robot-targeted content.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative measurement establishing substantial robot-targeted web content, followed by dated training records showing whether subsequent models ingest and learn from it, together with a comparable production-capacity assessment.
